multibyte.label: The message line that never ended
multibyte.explanation: The screen row holds eighty characters, one of them two bytes wide, so the text needs eighty-one bytes plus its terminator - one byte past the wide-count limit the conversion used. The original truncates exactly at the limit and writes no terminator, and the caller measures the buffer as a string: with the buffer junked and no zero anywhere, the measurement runs through all thousand twenty-four stale bytes. The correction bounds the conversion by the size of the caller buffer, so the full text converts and terminates at eighty-one.

wide.label: A wide terminal: 301 columns of four-byte text
wide.explanation: The message line is read the way the Borg reads it: the full terminal width (three hundred characters here, each four bytes in UTF-8) into a 1024-byte buffer followed by a guard area. The original limit of one byte per character stops after seventy-five characters without a terminator: unterminated, but nothing written past the buffer. The earlier fix shape, a limit of MB_CUR_MAX bytes per character, is not tied to the buffer: it writes 1201 bytes, 177 of them past the buffer (AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow). The buffer-size bound converts the 255 characters that fit, terminates at 1020 and writes nothing past the buffer.
